key_insight: LM-SimBench unifies LLM training simulation evaluation so researchers can compare prediction accuracy, configuration selection, and error sources across simulators.
engineering_relevance: Simulation can reduce reliance on costly distributed training trials when selecting parallelization strategies.
method: Decompose simulation into functional stages from model compilation to schedule-level aggregation.
Connect execution representations and cost estimators to measurable evaluation targets.
Profile workloads across five parallelism dimensions and activation recomputation.
evidence_signal: The dataset covers 348 feasible configurations across 23 model settings from 10 dense and MoE LLM families on an Ascend NPU cluster, with representative simulator evaluations and matched GPU–NPU experiments.
watch_item: Cross-platform experiments support applicability, but prediction accuracy and configuration rankings should be validated on target hardware and workloads.
paper_title: LM-SimBench: A Unified Framework, Dataset, and Benchmark for Large Language Model Training Simulation
